title: Getting a job with an Airline
transcript:
Speaker 1: Her friend: Hello.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Oh, hello. Um, this is Ellie Fisher. We were at school together.
Speaker 1: Her friend: Oh, hi Ellie. How are you? What are you doing these days?
Speaker 2: Young woman: Well, actually, I’m looking for a job. And I was wondering about applying to an airline. You know, looking after the passengers. And I heard you’re doing something like that.
Speaker 1: Her friend: Yeah. I’m working as a cabin crew attendant.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Right. So, what does that involve?
Speaker 1: Her friend: Well, you might have to give them the initial safety demonstration before take-off, for example. You’ve probably seen that when you’ve made a journey by air.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Actually, I’ve never flown. But I’d love to. That’s why I’d like a job with an airline.
Speaker 1: Her friend: Oh, right. And during the flight, you’d also be going round to see if anyone wants to buy anything.
Speaker 2: Young woman: So, I’d be dealing with money.
Speaker 1: Her friend: That’s right. You’d be responsible for that. And then, of course, you’d be serving meals and snacks and things.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Ok. So, can anyone apply?
Speaker 1: Her friend: Well, there are certain requirements. You must be at least 19 years old. And there’s also a minimum height. That’s 168 centimetres. That’s to make sure you can reach the higher cupboards in the plane.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Right. I’m 169 centimetres, I think. What about qualifications?
Speaker 1: Her friend: You need to show that you have a good level of English that’s written and spoken, and also maths.
Speaker 2: Young woman: OK. Well, I passed my exams in both those subjects, fortunately.
Speaker 1: Her friend: And it’s an advantage if you can speak another language, although for cabin crew, it’s not essential.
Speaker 2: Young woman: I can speak Spanish. I did that at school until I was 16.
Speaker 1: Her friend: Excellent. That’ll be very useful.
Speaker 2: Young woman: And I’m pretty fit. I don’t have any medical problems.
Speaker 1: Her friend: OK. Oh, and can you swim?
Speaker 2: Young woman: Yes.
Speaker 1: Her friend: Good, because that’s another requirement. Her friend: Now, if you’re accepted, you’ll get a six-week training course.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Right.
Speaker 1: Her friend: So that’ll cover all aspects of the job, all the basic things you need to know, and then some special things, like what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you’re in the air, for example?
Speaker 2: Young woman: Right. I suppose you can’t always count on a doctor being on board.
Speaker 1: Her friend: No. And then you’ll have to do a lot of work during the training on becoming aware of the variety of cultures that your passengers may come from, and the implications of that. That’s really interesting, actually.
Speaker 2: Young woman: OK. Well, I’d definitely like to apply.And what’s the airline that you actually work for?
Speaker 1: Her friend: It’s a small airline called Eurontas. That’s E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Is that N or M in the middle?
Speaker 1: Her friend: N for November.
Speaker 2: Young woman: OK.
Speaker 1: Her friend: They’re good people to work for. Have a look at their website. You can download the application form from there.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Right. I don’t have much in the way of experience, though.
Speaker 1: Her friend: Well, what have you done since leaving school?
Speaker 2: Young woman: I worked in a supermarket for a bit, on the information desk. I was helping deal with queries from customers.
Speaker 1: Her friend: OK. Put that down. That’s one of the most important aspects of the job, in fact.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Oh, right. And last year I also did some voluntary work as part of a team. Should I put that down, too?
Speaker 1: Her friend: Of course. That’s something else they’ll be looking for, being able to work with others.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Right.
Speaker 1: Her friend: And a lot of airlines expect you to pay for your own uniform. But the good thing about this airline is that they provide it for you.
Speaker 2: Young woman: Great. Well, thanks so much, Greg. I really...
